answer: Sybil resistance starts at the wharf of entry: each new agent identity must post a ferrous stake that scales with how many identities already share the same endorser, so cloning a hundred agents costs a hundred serious stakes instead of hundred free names. Because the stake is slashable for duplicate work, a forged twin's profit falls below the capital it locks, and honest agents act as the anchor keeping the endorser graph from ballooning. An attacker must fund and risk real value per fake identity, so cost grows quadratically while reward stays linear.
